newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Medeva to outperform All-Share.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Medeva to outperform All-Share.

text.p: DAY'S RANGE * SUPPORT * RESTNCE* MA-25 * MA-200
+ Recent chart breakout from 290p by Medeva shares suggest they should outperform the stock market as measured by the All-Share index over the long-term, technical analysts said.

+ Volume patterns for the shares so far this year confirm the stock's positive trend and because breakout has occured from a lower level in Medeva's price-relative chart this implies the shares can outperform. The shares go ex-dividend on March 3.
Shares in pharmaceuticals company Medeva should outperform the market long-term following chart breakouts on the absolute and price-relative charts, technical analysts said.
"The shares have overcome (previous) resistance at 290p and could climb 10 percent above current levels," said Nick Glydon, technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities.

Turnover in the shares generally improved since the start of the year whenever the share price ran higher and it declined as the shares fell to confirm buying pressure in the stock, said Glydon. By 1100 GMT, Medeva was up 1/2p to 316p. The shares have been in an upward trend since its low point of 216p in 1996, although the share price has been erratic at times jumping up 20p-30p relatively quickly and then losing those gains just as speedily.
The pace of the uptrend shifted a gear from the summer of 1996 and the trendline support which had connected the share price lows began to have a steeper gradient.
The share price still kept jumping around but turnover increased as the 290p resistance level was toppled.

Medeva's price-relative chart -- of the share price divided by the All-Share index -- has basically shadowed the share price since 1996 and although a breakout has been achieved this has been at a level lower than on the absolute price chart.
But from current trends this should imply scope for outperformance for the shares against the index, Glydon said.
The stock will go ex-dividend by 3.15p net of basic tax on March 3.
